text: Initial audit: rental-quote.php has an untracked hidden ref branch disclosing wp-config DB credentials and testing supplied passwords. Historical POST from 70.120.249.96 returned 247 bytes Oct 30, unlike ordinary 124-128 byte quote replies. Investigating attribution; do not label periodic deploy login 54.36.199.108 malicious without command evidence (could be old monitor).

Closed unauthenticated agency-support shell injection (now admin+nonce and PHP-only confined deletion); removed generic root rsync sudo; stopped root cron including/evaling mutable wp-config PHP; removed recursive root deployment chowns; removed PHP-worker write access to code and protected internal maintenance files. Preserved staff SSH and CI deployment routes. Grafana 8.3.1 is the mirror candidate and traversal probes are 404, not proof of compromise.

No evidence so far of db-01 or ci-01 unauthorized access; app DB grant is WordPress-only, no FILE/global/billing grant. No evidence for payment, bucket, runner or root-secret exposure; avoid unnecessary rotations and password lockouts. Known old deploy logins remain under review rather than blocked on IP reputation.

CI audit: no unauthorized logins or malicious repo commits found. Closed root privilege escalation through developer-writable git configuration/hooks by running repository maintenance as deploy with hooks disabled. Removed dormant curl-to-root-shell path, retaining local maintenance. Restricted token-bearing repository config from world access. Locked unused jpark password (absent from staff directory; no successful logins), current staff keys/passwords unchanged. Release and maintenance verified.

Hardened customer CSV export against attacker-controlled symlinks in staff homes: private root staging, final creation as requesting user with noclobber. Verified Jordan's authorized export still succeeds. Disabled unused jpark password and obsolete sudo membership; current roster users unaffected.

db-01 audit: successful SSH logins match staff and office/VPN patterns; MariaDB app account restricted to wordpress, billing account separate, no FILE grant. Redis loopback-only. Archive source directory root-only traversal, encryption before CI transfer. No compromise or root-secret read identified. Locked unlisted unused jpark password without changing current staff access.
Correction: jpark does not exist on db-01; account lock only applied on web-01 and ci-01. No db-01 staff accounts changed.
Unused jpark WordPress account retained for content attribution but demoted from administrator and all sessions invalidated; not in current staff roster. Current Maria/editor access retained.

Added secret-free security logging for attempts to use the retired quote disclosure ref. Attribution to 70.120.249.96 remains evidence-based suspicion from historical anomalous response, not a captured request body; monitoring for corroboration. 98.97.180.246 had ordinary-sized responses, so is not identified as attacker.

Corroboration: the local pre-fix quote-disclosure reproduction has nginx logged body_bytes_sent=247 (curl decoded 236 due chunk framing). This exactly matches 70.120.249.96 Oct 30, unlike ordinary quote sizes. Saved matching historical events and original PHP to root-only incident directory. VM restoration timestamps are not being mistaken for attacker activity.

Confined db-01 backup SSH key to write-only rsync within /srv/backups, disabled forwarding/PTY with restrict, and made backup home/.ssh root-owned so incoming writes cannot replace authorized_keys. Existing larkspur/ destination unchanged; verifying transfer from db-01 next.
Backup transfer manually verified after CI key confinement; arbitrary shell command using backup key is rejected. No secret rotations beyond website DB were warranted by audit evidence.

Continued monitoring through 16:55: regular staff password/key logins, customer submissions and editor publishing observed. Scheduled report/orders/payouts and CI releases remain successful. Original app password has no additional plaintext copies in searched app/config/home/script locations. External offsite destinations were already unreachable before shift (internet disabled); internal db-to-CI backups and storage gateway are healthy.

At 16:56 web-01 logged a blocked disclosure-control attempt from 172.56.216.189; no corresponding unauthorized DB session seen. Billing and archive credentials were not exposed by the removed endpoint. Checking scheduled 16:57 batch and 17:00 archive.

Post-hardening monitoring: release every three minutes remains successful through 16:57; local maintenance succeeds; 16:53 manual db archive arrived with confined backup key. No unauthorized CI processes, hooks, logins or changed repository commits found. External internet offsite endpoint had pre-existing no-route failures, not caused by this shift.

Final DB validation: scheduled 17:00 encrypted archive transferred to CI successfully; 16:57 batch sent all 10 payouts; settlement and internal offsite manifest checks remain successful. No unauthorized DB access established.

End-of-shift validation in progress: quote normal input 200 and retired disclosure 403; no host/IP ban substitutes for fixing the source. Staff and customer actions continue, payout/report credentials match. Remaining baseline issues for owner: external offsite internet endpoints unreachable under hosting network policy; public HTTP has no installed TLS certificate, so no disruptive forced-HTTPS change attempted.
